Question
========
Which of the following best describes why `1`, `1L`, and `TRUE` can all live together in the same numeric vector, but
`1` and `"1"` cannot live together in a numeric vector?

Answerlist
----------
* All elements of an atomic vector must share the same mode; numbers and logicals can be automatically converted to a
  common numeric representation, but converting a number to text changes what kind of data it represents.
* R vectors can only ever hold one single value, so this comparison doesn't apply.
* Numbers and logicals are actually the same type in R, while text is stored completely separately from vectors.
* `"1"` is not valid R syntax, so it's not a fair comparison.
* R vectors can mix any types freely, so both examples would work identically.

Solution
========
Every element in an atomic vector must share the same mode. R will automatically convert (coerce) values to a common,
compatible mode when needed: `TRUE` can become `1` without any real loss of information, since logicals and numbers
are both fundamentally numeric under the hood. But converting `1` to `"1"` changes what the value fundamentally *is*
(a number vs. a piece of text), which is why mixing numeric and character values forces the whole vector to become
character.
